Standard: The air vehicle provides the pilot with clear and unambiguous warnings and indications of less than 10% control margin remaining. For near-earth operations, the warnings and indications are interpretable by the pilot with eyes out of the cockpit. Special devices used for indication, warning, prevention, and recovery during normal or inadvertent operation do not create a hazard to the rotary-wing air vehicle. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Conduct analysis to assess that warnings and indications of less than 10% control margin remaining are clear and unambiguous to the pilot and that for near earth operations, the warnings and indications are interpretable by the pilot with their eyes focused outside of the cockpit. Verify that special devices, tactile cues (e.g., soft stops, stick shakers, stick pushers), haptic cues, and annunciations (aural and visual) that indicate, warn, prevent, or assist the pilot in recovering the air vehicle during normal or inadvertent operation do not create a hazard to the air vehicle. Test.
  (1) Lab test: Conduct piloted simulation and evaluation to assess that warnings and indications of less than 10% control margin remaining are clear and unambiguous to the pilot and that for near earth operations, the warnings and indications are interpretable by the pilot with their eyes focused outside of the cockpit. Verify that special devices, tactile cues (e.g., soft stops, stick shakers, stick pushers), haptic cues, and annunciations (aural and visual) that indicate, warn, prevent, or assist the pilot in recovering the air vehicle during normal or inadvertent operation do not create a hazard to the air vehicle. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
  (2) Flight test: Conduct flight test, for selected combinations of for all air vehicle configurations, loadings, and mission maneuvers within the SFE to assess that warnings and indications of less than 10% control margin remaining are clear and unambiguous to the pilot and that for near earth operations, the warnings and indications are interpretable by the pilot with their eyes focused outside of the cockpit. Verify that special devices, tactile cues (e.g., soft stops, stick shakers, stick pushers), haptic cues, and annunciations (aural and visual) that indicate, warn, prevent, or assist the pilot in recovering the air vehicle during normal or inadvertent operation do not create a hazard to the air vehicle.
